text:
toni: Heads-up: trying to add redwoodctl to our Docker-based quickstart for mac intel CI and hit installer weirdness. Homebrew bottle installs fine, but our pinned tarball install runs a postinstall that tries to launch the browser for auth and the job hangs.

lena: tarball install triggers `redwoodctl login` in postinstall? that's too eager. CI containers have no browser.

toni: yep. the packager added a healthcheck that runs `redwoodctl whoami` during postinstall and if not logged in it runs `redwoodctl login` to warm the cache. Not ok for noninteractive.

ash: simple mitigation: during CI set REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1 and do an explicit `redwoodctl login --token "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"` in a separate step. Also use `--unsafe-perm` for npm installs to avoid permission drops during postinstall.

toni: did that and it fixed the hang. hit a second thing: our sample-app looks for profiles at $PWD/.redwood first, then $HOME/.redwood, but the tarball installer wrote to /usr/local/etc/redwood which meant local-serve didn't pick up the token. Took a while to trace.

lena: that's bad defaulting. recommend honoring REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR env var if set and otherwise search a known list (explicitly printed) instead of guessing silently.

ash: +1. Also local-serve spawning behavior: when it tries to auth and calls `redwoodctl login` it doesn't forward our env (REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR), so child uses system default and creates a second profiles store. We ended up with two profiles and confusion.

toni: filed PDE-900: make local-serve pass --config-dir to spawned redwoodctl and inherit process env.

ci-bot: Note: CI best practice: set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR and REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN during image build; run `redwoodctl login --token` in a distinct step. See docs: https://internal.example.com/ci/redwoodctl-noninteractive

lena: another small but painful UX bug: when `redwoodctl login --device` runs in a CI log-less environment it prints the device URL only to stderr in the child process and local-serve didn't capture it, so engineers couldn't find the URL. We should always print device URLs to stdout and surface them in parent logs.

ash: agreed. also propose exit-code refinement: 20 = interactive-required (printed device URL), 21 = auth invalid (bad token), 22 = transient network. CI can retry only on 22.

toni: good taxonomy. I'll add it to the CLI RFC. Also propose a small Dockerfile snippet for the quickstart docs so new teams don't hit this:

```
FROM node:20-bullseye
ENV REDWOODCTL_SKIP_AUTOLOGIN=1
ENV REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=/workspace/.redwood
RUN npm ci -g --unsafe-perm redwoodctl
# later during setup step:
# echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | redwoodctl login --token -
```

lena: love it. last note: permissions on /usr/local when using rootless builds cause symlink EEXIST/EACCES on some runner images. `mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && chown node:node /usr/local/bin` before global installs helped.

devex-bot: PDE-900 created: pass config-dir to spawned CLI, print device URL in parent logs, and add exit-code taxonomy. Docs PR suggested for quickstart Dockerfile snippet.

toni: thanks everyone. i'll open the PR to update the installer to avoid auto-login during postinstall and to document the Docker snippet. closing thread once docs merged. :rocket:
